lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: a put-away system

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 2: Clothing and Laundry Care
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice a put-away system. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: You look at how your own clothes actually end up scattered around your space and design a simple put-away system, for one specific category, that you think would work better.
materials: learner-local: a small set of your own clothing to test the system on
learner-local: paper or a notes app to sketch or write your system
learner-local: your space's existing storage (drawers, shelves, hooks, bins)

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain the one specific change you made to fix the biggest problem, and predict whether this revised system would still work if the number of items in that category doubled.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System specificity and real trial: A specific category and a specific real spot are named with a real reason, and the system is tried on at least three real items. | Diagnosing and revising the problem: A specific, real problem from the trial is identified and tied to a specific revision that would fix it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design a second put-away system for a different category of their own clothing and compare, in writing, which of the two categories was harder to design a working system for and why.

resources.title: a put-away system worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: You look at how your own clothes actually end up scattered around your space and design a simple put-away system, for one specific category, that you think would work better.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact a put-away system decision or action.
Model move 2: Before designing anything, look at one category of your own clothing that tends to end up in the wrong place or in a pile.
Model move 3: Design a simple put-away system for that one category: decide exactly where each type of item in that category should live and why that spot makes sense.

Model check: System specificity and real trial: A specific category and a specific real spot are named with a real reason, and the system is tried on at least three real items. | Diagnosing and revising the problem: A specific, real problem from the trial is identified and tied to a specific revision that would fix it.

resources.title: a put-away system action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for a put-away system.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: a put-away system coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: You look at how your own clothes actually end up scattered around your space and design a simple put-away system, for one specific category, that you think would work better.
Coach direction: Before designing anything, look at one category of your own clothing that tends to end up in the wrong place or in a pile.
Learner prompt: Name the category and describe where those items usually end up instead of where they should go.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: a put-away system complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Design a simple put-away system for that one category: decide exactly where each type of item in that category should live and why that spot makes sense.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named one specific category, not 'all my clothes.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): I chose a specific real spot for the category and wrote down the reason that spot makes sense, such as easy to reach, easy to see, or close to where I get dressed.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I tried my system on at least three real items today.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: a put-away system minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain the one specific change you made to fix the biggest problem, and predict whether this revised system would still work if the number of items in that category doubled.

Success checks: System specificity and real trial: A specific category and a specific real spot are named with a real reason, and the system is tried on at least three real items. | Diagnosing and revising the problem: A specific, real problem from the trial is identified and tied to a specific revision that would fix it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: a put-away system supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional a put-away system condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — System specificity and real trial: A specific category and a specific real spot are named with a real reason, and the system is tried on at least three real items. | Diagnosing and revising the problem: A specific, real problem from the trial is identified and tied to a specific revision that would fix it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: a put-away system — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the a put-away system task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u02-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System specificity and real trial: A specific category and a specific real spot are named with a real reason, and the system is tried on at least three real items. | Diagnosing and revising the problem: A specific, real problem from the trial is identified and tied to a specific revision that would fix it.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
